For this reason I was wondering if it is alright to tell the person to 1. not make such excessive minnats that you can't fulfill yourself 2. to pray or carry out the good deed before you make the duaa (since making minnat is sort of like playing with allah). answer: Prayers & Duties >> Oaths & Vows Question ID: 33318 Country: India Title: May I know, how many Kaffarahs a person needs to give when he or she does not know how many times a promise have been broken? Question: May I know, how many Kaffarahs a person needs to give when he or she does not know how many times a promise have been broken? (The person tried to recall, but he was unable to conclude as the promise was broken many times). Answer ID: 33318 Posted on: Aug 31, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 1161/971/B=1432) He should have over-estimation of all oaths that he has broken and should give the kaffarah of the estimated oaths. Likelihood shall be in place of surety. Just what is likelihood, it is enough. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
